sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Nayak,Vijyant

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
None appears for the complainant despite service of notice.

2. It is argued by the counsel for the applicant that F.I.R. was lodged as a missing person report subsequently, the victim aged about 17 years did not support the prosecution story and stated that she has married with the applicant.
Applicant is in jail since 22.04.2024 however, he has no criminal antecedent.
3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

sentences.text: 4. Considering the overall facts as stated above and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant- Soojal be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.068 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Ibrahimpur, District Ambedkar Nagar, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.7.2024 Saurabh Yadav/-
